Manufacturers: same as applicant (Applicant and Manufacturer), so include the same entry.

Certified type:
- Category: Non-automatic weighing instrument → category "Non-automatic weighing instrument" (schema says category examples: "Load cell", "Indicator", ... — I'll use "Non-automatic weighing instrument")
- Type designations: ["S-boxM series"] — the type is "S-boxM series". Should I extract "S-boxM" as model family? The type designation is "S-boxM series". The cert covers Max from 3 kg to 30 kg. Hmm, is that a model family? The Max is given as a range 3 kg ≤ Max ≤ 30 kg — this could mean the series covers capacities from 3 kg to 30 kg. But there's no explicit model table. I could treat this as a range in type_level. Rule 4 says detect families with comma-separated values or 2-D tables. Here it's a range, so keep as type_level with {min: 3, max: 30}, unit kg.

Characteristics:
- Accuracy class: (III) → accuracy_classes in recommendation: ["III"]. Also could be type_level characteristic "accuracy_class": "III".
- Maximum capacity: 3 kg ≤ Max ≤ 30 kg → {min: 3, max: 30}, unit kg
- Verification scale interval: e ≥ 1 g → {min: 1, max: null}, unit g
- Weighing range: Single interval → string value "Single interval"
- Maximum number of scale intervals: n ≤ 3000 → {min: null, max: 3000}, dimensionless
- Temperature range: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit °C
- Power supply voltage: 9 V DC through plug-in power supply; 6 V DC with internal rechargeable battery; 7,5 V DC with dry battery. This is interesting — three configurations:
  - plug-in power supply: 9 V DC
  - internal rechargeable battery: 6 V DC
  - dry battery: 7.5 V DC
  
  This could be config_level with axis "power_source" with conditions: "plug-in power supply" → 9 V, "internal rechargeable battery" → 6 V, "dry battery" → 7.5 V. Or type_level power_supply_voltage as list? Rules say lists of values become model matrices... but these aren't models, they're power supply configurations. Config level fits well: axis "power_source".
  
  I'll do both: config_level entries with attribute "power_supply_voltage", axis "power_source", values with conditions. Note 7,5 → 7.5 decimal fix.

- Software identification: 2.yy.xxxx (y, x = 0…9) → string value "2.yy.xxxx" — maybe type_level "software_identification": {"value": "2.yy.xxxx"}. The "(y, x = 0…9)" is explanation. I can include it as value string "2.yy.xxxx" and maybe note. I'll keep value as "2.yy.xxxx".

Recommendation:
- id: R76 (canonical), edition: 2006? The recommendation is "OIML R 76-1:2006". Hmm. R76-1:2006. Canonical id "R76", edition 2006. But it's R76-1 — part 1. The schema has id, edition, amendment, scheme, accuracy_classes. I'll use id "R76", edition 2006. Maybe include "part": not in schema; skip. Actually could I put id "R76-1"? The rule says canonical e.g. "R60" not "OIML R 60". For R76-1, canonical might be "R76-1". I'll use "R76-1" to be precise since the certificate specifically says R 76-1:2006. Hmm, the guidance example transforms "OIML R 60" → "R60". "R76-1" is the actual designation. I'll go with "R76-1". Edition: 2006. Scheme: "A". accuracy_classes: ["III"].

The Max range is a range, not a list. I think type_level with range value is appropriate; omit model_family (include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant — here variants aren't explicitly enumerated). Hmm, but the range 3-30 kg could mean multiple capacities... but no explicit models listed. Rule 8: don't fabricate. I'll omit model_family.
